draft.title: Non-government organisations
card: A non-government organisation (NGO) is a group that is not part of any government. It works to improve people's lives rather than to make a profit.
NGOs raise money from donations, such as gifts from the public, and from sponsors, such as businesses. Some also receive grants from governments.
NGOs use this money to run programs that improve wellbeing. Examples are clean water projects, schools and health clinics.
World Vision is an NGO. It works with local communities in many countries, including in Asia and the Pacific.
draft.remember: NGOs are non-profit groups outside government that raise money and run programs to improve wellbeing.

a.q: Which description best fits an NGO such as World Vision?
opts: A group outside government that runs programs for wellbeing
A government agency that collects taxes to fund programs
A business that sells goods to earn profit for its owners
A government department that sets laws for other countries
a.why: An NGO is not part of a government and works to improve lives, not to make a profit. A government agency is the tempting wrong answer, because it also funds programs, but it is part of a government.
a.clue: Think about who runs the group and why it exists.

b.q: A group in Perth collects donations from the public. It uses the money to build wells and a school in a village in Timor-Leste. Why is it an NGO?
opts: It is outside government and runs programs for wellbeing
It receives all of its money directly from taxes
It aims to make a profit from the village it helps
It was set up by the Timor-Leste government
b.why: The group is separate from any government and uses donations to run programs that improve wellbeing. Receiving money from taxes is wrong because the card says NGOs raise money from donations and sponsors, and some may also receive grants.
b.clue: Look at who the group is, where its money comes from and what it does.

a.best: A group outside government that runs programs for wellbeing

b.best: It is outside government and runs programs for wellbeing

problems.detail: The why's reason for rejecting the taxes option is muddled. Government grants are funded by taxes, and the why itself says some NGOs receive grants. The real reasons the option is wrong are that the group in the question is funded by public donations, and that the option says 'all' of its money comes from taxes. As written, the why could confuse students about whether NGOs can receive tax-funded money.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The why for (b) gives a confusing reason for rejecting the taxes option, since grants are themselves tax-funded; it should point to the donations in the scenario and the word 'all'.
